subject: VitalityBio — data deletion scope, escrow evidence & SIG/CAIQ gap items
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@vitalitybio.it>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: vitality-compliance@vitalitybio.com
Date: 2028-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question: data deletion scope + escrow evidence for SIG review

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The compliance team is working through the SIG/CAIQ mapping and we have two follow-ups specific to our regulated workflows:

1) Our legal need: if a tenant requests data deletion (SAR-driven), can Redwood provide a cryptographic proof-of-delete and an export manifest that identifies which log tiers were affected (debug/tracing/ephemeral inference traces)? We need to show a chain of custody back to the S3/object deletion for audits.

2) Escrow/forensics: for customers who request a temporary retention carveout (30–90 days) for legal hold, what evidence artifacts does Redwood provide to attest that only the scoped tenant traces were preserved and later removed? We need a list of deliverables (e.g., signed manifest, snapshot hashes, deletion timestamps).

We're preparing internal SIG notes and would like to include concrete filenames and an example artifact so our auditors can see the format. Can you point us to an example export and confirm whether Redwood supports tenant-scoped immutable snapshots?

Appreciate a short list of artifacts and a timeline for producing them.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Compliance, VitalityBio
Elena.Rossi@vitalitybio.it
+39 02 1234 5678

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@vitalitybio.it>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: data deletion scope + escrow evidence for SIG review

Elena —

Short answer: yes, we can produce tenant-scoped export manifests and time-stamped proofs of deletion. Below is what we typically provide and an example delivery timeline. I'll copy Stephanie (CS ops) and Priyom (security/forensics) for technical specifics.

Deliverables we can produce:
- export_manifest.csv: lists tenant_id, export_object_key, sequence_range, produced_at (ISO8601), signer_id
- snapshot_hashes.txt: SHA256 hashes of the archived snapshot tarballs (signed by Redwood KMS)
- proof_of_delete_manifest.csv: records deletion_object_key, deleted_by, deleted_at, purge_job_id, and KMS-signature reference
- sample_export.jsonl: redwood inference events (redacted PII) — for auditor formatting checks
- audit_chain_report.pdf: human-readable mapping of actions + links to the S3/escrow vault record (if escrow requested)

Retention carveout (temporary hold) flow we follow:
1) Customer requests carveout via support/console with explicit tenant_id and hold window.
2) We snapshot tenant artifacts to a write-once escrow bucket (customer-managed or Redwood-managed per contract).
3) We provide signed snapshot_hashes and an export_manifest within 48–72 hours.
4) At end of hold, we perform deletion jobs which emit proof_of_delete_manifest and make the deletion job id available for auditor retrieval.

Timing: standard request -> artifacts in 2–3 business days; proof_of_delete after deletion job completes (typically within 24 hours of purge).

Questions for you:
- Do you prefer Redwood to place escrow snapshots into a VitalityBio-controlled S3 bucket (we support cross-account writes) or into Redwood-managed escrow (we provide signed attestations)?
- Any special retention extended beyond 90 days?

We can provide a sample export this week. Priyom / Stephanie — can you confirm the exact artifact filenames and whether we should include KMS-signature blobs inline or as separate signature files?

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Customer Security — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

On Apr 11, 2028, at 09:50, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Markus — we include KMS signatures as separate .sig files (one per tarball) and reference them in the manifest. For escrow to customer S3 we deliver via presigned multipart upload and include the upload manifest ci-checksum.
> Stephanie

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@vitalitybio.it>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: vitality-compliance@vitalitybio.com
Date: 2028-04-12T07:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: data deletion scope + escrow evidence for SIG review

Markus — thanks, that level of detail is helpful. VitalityBio would prefer cross-account escrow: we will provide an S3 bucket and IAM write role so snapshots live in our control during the hold. Two follow-ups:

- For the proof_of_delete_manifest, our auditors ask for a chain-of-custody that includes the user who initiated the deletion (support agent or system job) and the job id. Will the deleted_by field include system actor identities and system job ids?
- On sampling: can you provide a 5k-line sample of the export (redacted) to demonstrate format, plus SIG answers for the CAIQ items we flagged (we've attached a short list).

Attached: Vitality_SIG_flagged_items.xlsx (we referenced specific CAIQ controls where we need clarifications).

If you can confirm by EOD Monday, we will slot the escrow setup next week.

Best,
Elena

> Priyom
